public_rationale: The specific comparison holds. Ordinary forgetting involves failures of attention, encoding or retrieval; the LLM experiments document generation of false assertions, including assertions the same model can separately reject. These are different characteristic errors and processes. This is a synthesis of separate research, not a direct comparative experiment. It does not support a broader claim that human and LLM errors never resemble one another.
limitations: Support depends on retaining the explicit car-keys comparison.
The mechanism distinction is inferred from separate research programs.
Humans also exhibit constructive memory distortions.

our_interpretation: Assess the mechanism comparison as causal, despite the supplied observation label.
Read the comparison narrowly: generating unsupported factual content versus ordinary failure to encode or retrieve an object's location.
Do not expand this into a claim that humans never fabricate, or that human and LLM errors have no shared abstract features.
The qualitative distinction is invention of asserted content versus failure to remember an experienced event.
criteria.support_condition: Research distinguishes the processes and characteristic outputs of ordinary episodic forgetting from those producing LLM factual inventions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes the same relevant process and characteristic error for LLM fabrication and ordinary forgetting of an object's location.

evidence.explanation: The review separates failures to remember from memory distortions. Its absent-mindedness section describes attention and retrieval-cue failures, supporting the human side of the narrow process comparison.

The experiments document false assertions generated in support of an earlier answer, despite the models' ability to reject those assertions separately. Together with the memory review, this supports an inferred distinction from ordinary failure to remember an object's location.
The review nevertheless documents induced human recollections of suggested events. Thus the narrow forgetting comparison cannot establish that all human and LLM errors are qualitatively distinct.
